objective: Implement the Codex-Claude Supervisor Bridge exactly per the captured D-007 directive (source-001.md, digest 426da3bb): Phase 1 core loop (schemas, models, config incl. acceptance_scenarios: AS-1 (executable): the Section 16 acceptance criteria 1-16 each pass at one frozen SHA with independent code (G3), security (G5), and control-plane reviews; all repository tests and CI green.

AS-2 (executable): the Section 15 test matrix runs green with fake Claude/Codex executables - parsing/process, state-machine, tier-policy, model-selection, approval-broker, evidence, rotation, recovery/scheduling, adversarial-essentials, and historical-replay suites all present and passing; no real tokens by default.

AS-3 (executable): tier-policy invariant tests prove every Section 13.12 invariant (1-15), including: no owner gate satisfied by a model, no automatic merge/deploy/credential/payment/G6, no reviewer write access, no worker access to the active controller, HARD-DENY immovable by both models.

AS-4: the audit log hash chain (mandatory) detects tampering, truncation, and reordering in seeded tests; the external-anchoring decision is implemented as the owner ruled it at dispatch (or its deferral carries the owner+security-review acceptance D-007 Section 13.12 requires).

AS-5 (executable): replay mode reproduces expected stop/continue behavior on the agreed historical corpus (M0-T031 lifecycle, B-015 sentinel failure, M0-T028 detection-only stop, a clean continuation, a correction, a CI failure, a stale-SHA case, an owner-gated stop).

AS-6: shadow mode completes at least one real controlled-task lifecycle within the owner-touch budget (default <= 2 would-be synchronous stops, excluding activation), every excess stop dispositioned; the run ends AT the merge/acceptance gate, never past it.

AS-7 (containment): git diff --name-only touches only allowed_paths; no .claude/, .github/, or product change; no effort key anywhere; no bypass flag anywhere in code, tests, or docs except as HARD-DENY list constants.
AS-8: limited-auto remains disabled at task end; activation is a separate explicit owner act recorded through directive compliance (D-007 Section 12).
risks: Scale: D-007 spans 5 phases; the packet authorizes Phases 1-4 + the Phase 5 shadow pilot, with the activation decision owner-gated. Split into per-phase follow-up tasks at the orchestrator's discretion if a phase exceeds a safe review size - contract splits through the normal process, never widen this packet.
Windows process-tree control (Job Objects) and durable Task Scheduler wake are the highest-uncertainty areas; Section 18 stop conditions apply if a safe strategy cannot be proven.

The worker/controller isolation requirement (Section 13.1/13.3) needs an execution location decision from the owner at dispatch: a dedicated read-only controller checkout outside every Claude-writable path.
codex-cli/claude-cli version drift between Phase 0 verification (codex 0.146.0, claude native 2.1.220) and dispatch time: preflight reverifies every flag on the pinned binaries (Section 8.5/13.4).
